result.instructions: Two tools for the running desktop. AX reads and operates application windows through accessibility: it lists windows, returns controls as rN refs, acts on them, and waits with wait steps. GUI takes full-desktop screenshots and sends pixel input. Use AX for named controls, values, menus, dialogs, windows, and keys. Use GUI for pixels, canvases, dragging, and controls that AX does not expose; after one targeted AX find misses a visible control, use GUI for it. Send all desktop input (window activation, keys, text, mouse) through these tools, not shell input utilities or scripted accessibility calls: the tools check the target window before input and report what changed, and outside input makes their refs and diffs stale. After GUI input, read AX again before reusing refs.

query.description: At least one filter; ANDed, case-insensitive.

actions.description: act: ordered steps; a failed step stops the batch. Wait timeouts total at most 60000 ms; an omitted timeout counts as 5000 ms.

ref.description: rN element; wN for activate/close. Omit for keys/text to the focused window.

settle.description: wait: true waits until the UI changes after the step before it, then stops changing.

text.description: wait: text in the ref element, or anywhere in the window. select: substring of ref to select.

title.description: activate/close: unique window-title substring, instead of wN.

to_ref.description: select: range end; ref..to_ref spans text or cells.

window.description: wait: a top-level window whose title contains this, on the whole desktop.

app.description: App name, app id, or PID; use once, then window_ref.

cursor.description: find: next_cursor from a truncated result; send with mode find only.

mode.description: apps lists confirmed top-level windows (wN, title, app, active) and reports incomplete inventories; observe returns a tree or diff with rN; find returns matching rN; act runs actions.

observe.description: Returned evidence. act: default diff; explicit tree returns the complete window tree, full adds the full-desktop GUI screenshot. observe: default tree. none only with act.

root.description: observe: subtree at rN or the focused element.

window_ref.description: observe/find: window to read. act: omit when actions have refs, which name the window; it only sends ref-less keys/text to wN instead of the focused window.

tools.name: AX
tools.title: Accessibility

tools.description: Full-desktop screenshot and pixel input. {"actions":[{"type":"screenshot"}]} alone observes; {"type":"zoom","region":[x0,y0,x1,y1]} alone enlarges a frame region to read small text and icons. Any other batch is checked before input and returns one final screenshot. x/y are pixels of the latest full-desktop image (screen width x height) from GUI or AX full/screenshot, which return the same frame. type/keypress go to the current focus, so click the field first. Batch the actions planned from one screenshot; end the batch after an action that may open, close, or move a window, and plan the rest from the returned image. GUI cannot address windows; AX activates and closes them by title. wait is one second with no observation, at most 20 s per batch. Errors return code and hint like AX; gui_frame_stale means nothing was sent: replan from the returned screenshot. Example: {"actions":[{"type":"click","x":640,"y":412},{"type":"type","text":"hello"},{"type":"keypress","keys":["ENTER"]}]}

inputSchema.description: One screenshot or zoom action observes; otherwise run an input batch.

type.description: Capture the final full desktop; this must be the only action.
Look only: enlarge a frame region; alone.

x.description: X pixel in the exact returned full-desktop image

y.description: Y pixel in the exact returned full-desktop image

type.description: Wait exactly one second without an intermediate observation; do not stack waits.

settle_ms.description: Visual stillness: default 800ms, max 3000ms. Final screenshot stillness, not semantic success and not extra sleep. After wait, usually omit it. At the cap inspect the screenshot or use an AX wait step.

cli.--help:
Computer Use

Usage:
  computer-use [command] [options]

Commands:
  mcp                  Start the stdio MCP server.
  doctor               Print platform runtime requirements.
  call <AX|GUI>         Call one public tool, or run a JSON array of calls.
  help [command]       Show general or command-specific help.
  version              Print the CLI version.

Notes:
  Run in the signed-in desktop session. Native providers use Linux AT-SPI2,
  macOS Accessibility, or Windows UI Automation. Run doctor for requirements.
cli.help call:
Usage:
  computer-use call <AX|GUI> [--args '<json-object>']
  computer-use call --calls '<json-array>'

Only the public AX and GUI tools are accepted.
